title: Philippines Revamps International Co-Production Fund With Minority and Majority Tracks, Unveiled at Busan Market
content:
ByNaman Ramachandran

ThePhilippineshas revamped its International Co-Production Fund (ICOF) around two tracks, with the amount of cash on offer tied to the size of the Filipino stake in a project.

The Film Philippines Office (FPO) unveiled the new framework at theBusan International Film Festival‘s Asian Contents & Film Market.

The Majority Track covers projects led by Filipino producers working with foreign partners. Features and series on this track can receive up to PHP13 million ($210,000), and documentaries and shorts up to PHP5 million ($80,000).

To qualify, the Filipino side must own at least 20% of the project and hold the largest share among the co-producers. Two Filipinos must fill above-the-line roles – director, writer or actor – and five more must work in key creative or technical crew positions. Applicants need a release strategy for both the home market and abroad. Foreign partners must take a minority stake and make a matching creative or technical contribution.

The Minority Track is for international productions in which a Filipino producer is the junior partner. Features and series can draw up to PHP7 million ($113,000), with documentaries and shorts capped at PHP3 million ($48,000).

The bar is lower here. Filipino producers need a stake of 10% or more, and the production must hire either two Filipino above-the-line talents or three Filipino crew members in key creative or technical roles. Applicants must also show how the film will reach audiences outside the Philippines.

Both tracks offer the same top-ups. Qualifying ASEAN co-productions earn an extra PHP1 million ($16,000), and projects that clear a cultural test can collect up to PHP2 million ($32,000) more. The FPO noted that the dollar figures may vary with exchange rates.

The FPO sits within the Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP), the national film agency that reports to the Office of the President. It runs the country’s incentives for international co-productions and for line and post-production work. It also provides endorsements for government permits and makes location referrals.

Several ICOF-backed films have won festival prizes. Tommy Ng Ka Chung’s “Another World” was co-produced by Filipino company Overmind Corp with partners in Hong Kong and Singapore, and won best animated feature at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in November 2025. Janus Victoria’s “Diamonds in the Sand,” which has Japanese and Malaysian co-producers, took the Mulberry Award for best debut film at Udine’s Far East Film Festival.

Marianne Métivier’s “Elsewhere at Night” won best screenplay at the Torino Film Festival. James J. Robinson picked up best Australian director at the Melbourne International Film Festival for “First Light.” Mouly Surya’s “This City Is a Battlefield” won best cinematography at the Bandung Film Festival.

The FPO’s separate Film Location Incentive Program has backed two prizewinners. Rafael Manuel’s “Filipiñana” won a special jury award for creative vision in Sundance’s World Cinema Dramatic competition, and Morgan Knibbe’s “The Garden of Earthly Delights” won best film at Torino.
title_zh: 菲律賓在釜山市場公布了國際合拍基金的改革計劃，該計劃包括少數和多數兩個追蹤項目。
content_zh:
由納曼·拉馬昌德蘭(Naman Ramachandran)報導

菲律賓已經重新調整了其國際合拍基金(International Co-Production Fund, ICOF)，分為兩個路徑，提供的資金數額與菲律賓在項目中的股份大小相關。

菲律賓電影辦公室(Film Philippines Office, FPO)在釜山國際電影節(Busan International Film Festival)的亞洲內容與電影市場上揭示了這一新框架。

主要路徑(Majority Track)涵蓋由菲律賓製片人與外國合作夥伴共同主導的項目。這一路徑上的長片和系列可以獲得高達1300萬比索(PHP 13 million, 約210,000美元)，而紀錄片和短片則可獲得高達500萬比索(PHP 5 million, 約80,000美元)。

為了符合資格，菲律賓方面必須擁有至少20%的項目股份，並在合製片人中持有最大的股份。兩名菲律賓人必須擔任主要角色——導演、編劇或演員——並且還需有五名以上的菲律賓人在關鍵創意或技術工作崗位上工作。申請者需要提供針對本國市場和國外市場的發行策略。外國合作夥伴必須持有少數股份並作出相應的創意或技術貢獻。

少數路徑(Minority Track)則適用於菲律賓製片人為次要合作夥伴的國際製作。長片和系列可以獲得高達700萬比索(PHP 7 million, 約113,000美元)，而紀錄片和短片的上限為300萬比索(PHP 3 million, 約48,000美元)。

這裡的門檻較低。菲律賓製片人需要持有10%或以上的股份，並且製作必須聘用兩名菲律賓主要人才或三名菲律賓關鍵創意或技術崗位的工作人員。申請者還必須展示該影片如何觸及菲律賓以外的觀眾。

兩個路徑都提供相同的額外資金。符合資格的東盟(ASEAN)合拍片可獲得額外的100萬比索(PHP 1 million, 約16,000美元)，而通過文化測試的項目則可再獲得高達200萬比索(PHP 2 million, 約32,000美元)。FPO指出，美元數字可能會因匯率變化而有所不同。

FPO隸屬於菲律賓電影發展委員會(Film Development Council of the Philippines, FDCP)，這是向總統辦公室報告的國家電影機構。它負責該國的國際合拍和後期製作工作的激勵措施，還提供政府許可的推薦並進行地點推薦。

幾部由ICOF支持的電影已在影展上獲獎。湯米·吳嘉聰(Tommy Ng Ka Chung)的《另一個世界(Another World)》由菲律賓公司Overmind Corp與香港和新加坡的合作夥伴共同製作，並在2025年11月的第62屆金馬獎中獲得最佳動畫長片。雅努斯·維多利亞(Janus Victoria)的《沙中的鑽石(Diamonds in the Sand)》擁有日本和馬來西亞的合製片人，在烏迪內的遠東電影節上獲得最佳首部電影的桑葚獎(Mulberry Award)。

瑪麗安·梅蒂維耶(Marianne Métivier)的《夜晚的另一處(Elsewhere at Night)》在都靈電影節上獲得最佳劇本獎。詹姆斯·J·羅賓遜(James J. Robinson)在墨爾本國際電影節上因《第一道曙光(First Light)》獲得最佳澳大利亞導演獎。穆利·蘇里亞(Mouly Surya)的《這座城市是戰場(This City Is a Battlefield)》在萬丹電影節上獲得最佳攝影獎。

FPO的獨立電影拍攝地點獎勵計劃支持了兩部獲獎作品。拉斐爾·曼努埃爾(Rafael Manuel)的《菲律賓娜》(Filipiñana)在薩達斯(Sundance)的世界電影劇情競賽中獲得了創意視野特別評審獎，而摩根·尼布(Morgan Knibbe)的《人間樂園》(The Garden of Earthly Delights)則在都靈(Torino)獲得最佳影片獎。
